name: War
description: War is a simple children's card game. 2 players. 52-card deck split evenly. Both flip top card simultaneously — higher wins both. Tie = 'War': each plays 1 face-down then 1 face-up; higher face-up wins all. Continue until one player has all cards. Pure luck — no decisions.

history.origins: War is a children's comparison card game played in many parts of the world. No single inventor or date is documented; it has long been passed on as a first card game. In the United Kingdom it is often called Battle. Related regional forms include the Russian P'yanitsa (Drunkard), the German Tod und Leben (Life and Death), and Syrian War, indicating broad dissemination across Europe and beyond. The core mechanic—simultaneously revealing cards and the higher rank capturing both—is one of the simplest card-game structures and requires no strategy, only the ability to compare ranks.
timeline: 20th century: Documented as a children's comparison game in English-speaking and European sources.
history.cultural: Known worldwide as a first card game for children; played in North America, the UK, Europe, and elsewhere with local names and minor rule variants.
history.evolution: Universal children's first card game; regional variants (Russian Drunkard, German Tod und Leben, Syrian War) share the same flip-and-compare core.

setup.deck: 52 cards. A high. Split deck evenly 26-26.

rules.objective: Win all 52 cards by capturing the opponent's cards through comparison; the player who ends up with all the cards wins.
rules.gameplay: Both flip top card. Higher wins both (placed at bottom). Tie = War: 1 face-down then 1 face-up each. Higher face-up wins all cards in the war. Multiple wars possible. Insufficient cards during war = lose.

variations.name: Three face-down war
variations.description: In a war, each player plays three cards face down then one face up (ten cards total). Whoever has the higher face-up card wins all ten. If a player has fewer than four cards, some play that the player with fewest cards uses all their cards and the other plays the same number.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variation only changes war structure; no engine constant overrides needed for this summary.

variations.name: War with two jokers
variations.description: Two jokers are added to the pack and count as the highest cards, above aces. To avoid one player getting both, some separate the jokers before dividing the deck and bury one joker in each player's stack.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variation adds jokers; full implementation would require deck and rank overrides to be added later.

scoring.description: Win all cards or opponent runs out.
